name: PCCW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Jack Cole won it in an angle recapped rather than shown in this wing's own served corpus; Shane Douglas held it entering CaliQuake '97, where Tony Marconi dethroned him in the same segment that wrote Douglas out of PCCW; Marconi held it into December, surviving both a JUSTICE beatdown and his own staged double-cross of that same stable.

name: PCCW World Television Championship
epitaph: "Bad Attitude" Blade Dryden held it before CaliQuake '97's own four-way steel cage match crowned Ajax Shiva; Shiva lost it to the fWo's Paul-Dog on 7 December 1997 after interference from the Aerial Marauder.

name: PCCW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: New Jack and John Kronus lost the titles to Pain & Suffering (Sabre and Sledge Hammer of the Danger Zone Alliance) at CaliQuake '97; Pain & Suffering retained in a tables-strewn brawl at Jersey Jams, "our first title defense ever."

name: PCCW World Six-Man Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Held throughout this wing's own served corpus by JUSTICE's own "Law & Order" pairing and the Machine; no challenge for it resolves within this collection's holdings.

name: PCCW World Light Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: A comedy-billed lineage that changed hands repeatedly across 1997: Syxx lost it to Al Snow (wrestling as "Leif Cassidy"), who was upset by El Jobbo Grande within a week, who in turn lost it to Sean Southward -- the CaliQuake '97 commentary's own recap of "two former PCCW World light heavyweight champions" meeting in a non-title match. El Jobbo Grande is billed a 'former' champion again by Jersey Jams, where a first-round Light Heavyweight tournament match (Ultimo Warrior vs. an unminted opponent) runs toward a vacant or re-claimed title this collection's own holdings do not resolve.

name: PCCW Extreme Championship
epitaph: The Aerial Marauder is already champion entering this wing's own served corpus -- how or when he won the title does not survive in this collection's holdings -- and retains it against Raven at Jersey Jams with a staged assist from the World Heavyweight Champion.
